knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure says to choose equipment based on finish, soil type, access, contamination zone and manufacturer instructions.
The worked scenario rejects a stiff brush on a polished stone vanity, selects a soft compatible cloth and reports the remaining deposit.
The core procedure says to use separate tools for sanitary areas and food-contact surfaces.

practicalCriteria: Matches tools to surfaces and prevents cross-contamination and abrasion.
Explains applicable scope and site procedures
Demonstrates hazard controls and safe stop-work decisions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record covering procedure steps 1-7
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Choose a tool that suits the surface, and do not use abrasive tools on delicate finishes such as polished stone.
Stop work if procedure step 7 is not done: If the method, product or equipment is unsafe or uncertain, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.
